The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: MetricsAbsent on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: No metrics received from io-shop since 2026-11-11T02:46:00Z {A1} - 5m {A2} with no sample, against a scrape interval of 15 {A3} seconds. The series stopped rather than crossing a threshold, so nothing here says whether the shop is well: these minutes have no readings to judge, not readings that look bad.
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T02:51:47Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T02:51:53Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule fires as soon as its condition holds. The alert came 3 minutes 17 seconds {beyond_accounted_for} later than the 2 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the metrics' stopping is measured to. The record does not show what took the rest.
No metrics were collected from 2026-11-11T02:46:00Z {metrics_stopped_at} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute) until they resumed at 2026-11-11T02:52:32Z {metrics_resumed_at} (in the minute Argus acted in, so dated to its action), showing the service back to normal. That is 6 minutes 32 seconds {duration} the metrics did not cover, not a stretch the service is known to have spent in trouble.
Log lines read reach into it until 2026-11-11T02:51:00Z {logs_reach_until}: [G46bc], [Gbac1]. They are the service's own account of that stretch: what they report there is what is known of how it was doing, and up to then the service was seen through them. The logs were read up to 2026-11-11T02:51:00Z {log_reading_ended} - nothing after that was read.
How the service did over that stretch is said by the document itself, from your answer to logs_show_serving_as_before: say nothing of it anywhere else. Where the chain's first step says nobody using the service saw anything wrong, cite those log lines for it without saying what they show.
Argus held the incident for 1 minute 18 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T02:53:06Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
Error rate: not measured by the metrics - none were collected from when the metrics stopped until they resumed; the log lines that reach into that stretch, [G46bc], [Gbac1], are the service's own account of it, so do not say nothing was measured; what they show is said by the document itself, from your answer to logs_show_serving_as_before.
Customer loss: none - the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-11T02:51:47Z {T1.1} Argus: Received MetricsAbsent on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-11T02:52:00Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-11T02:52:00Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-11T02:52:11Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 02:51:47 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-11T02:52:15Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read the service's metrics - they stop after the minute at 02:45 {T5.2}, and nothing covers the minutes since
  - [T6] 2026-11-11T02:52:16Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 02:46 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-11T02:52:16Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-11T02:52:17Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 {T8.2} day 5 {T8.3} minutes 47 {T8.4} seconds before Nov 11 02:51:47 {T8.5}
  - [T9] 2026-11-11T02:52:18Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 2 {T9.2} production changes
  - [T10] 2026-11-11T02:52:18Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 7 {T10.2} minutes before 02:51 {T10.3}
  - [T11] 2026-11-11T02:52:19Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 21 {T11.2} log lines
  - [T12] 2026-11-11T02:52:25Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read what the deployment of 9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020 changed
  - [T13] 2026-11-11T02:52:26Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 3 {T13.2} candidate causes, best first: C1, C2, C3
  - [T14] 2026-11-11T02:52:26Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-11T02:52:26Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 0 {T15.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 02:52:26 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-11T02:52:30Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-11T02:52:30Z {T17.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T18] 2026-11-11T02:52:32Z {T18.1} Mitigation Agent: Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1
  - [T19] 2026-11-11T02:52:38Z {T19.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether its metrics can be read again, from 02:53 {T19.2} - up to 87s {T19.3}
  - [T20] 2026-11-11T02:53:06Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - its metrics could be read again from 02:52 {T20.2}
  - [T21] 2026-11-11T02:53:06Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T22] 2026-11-11T02:53:06Z {T22.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - rolled [io-shop] back off revision [9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020] and the service could be read again
  - [T23] 2026-11-11T02:54:44Z {T23.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/537

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-10T22:46:07Z {P1.1} deploy e283ba3af732fc4285166a060b827b1305cd30d9 by kuki: deployed revision e283ba3af732fc4285166a060b827b1305cd30d9 from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
  - [P2] 2026-11-11T02:46:07Z {P2.1} deploy 9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020 by kuki: deployed revision 9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020 from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
  - Flags read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - before the metrics stopped: 4 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 2 {G46bc.2} minutes, 02:44–02:45 {G46bc.3}. After they stopped: 9 {G46bc.4} occurrences in 6 {G46bc.5} minutes, 02:46–02:51 {G46bc.6}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - before the metrics stopped: 2 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 2 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 02:44–02:45 {Gbac1.3}; # was 1.50% {Gbac1.4}. After they stopped: 6 {Gbac1.5} occurrences in 6 {Gbac1.6} minutes, 02:46–02:51 {Gbac1.7}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.8} to 2.00% {Gbac1.9}, typically 0.50% {Gbac1.10}, highest at 02:51 {Gbac1.11}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1, also C2, C3] Candidates blaming the same move of metrics.portName, each reading it as a different kind of failure - different accounts of what it did, not one cause counted twice - each in its own words:
      C1: The service is still serving normally, but the metrics stopped. The deploy at 2026-11-11T02:46:07Z {C1.1} changed one value, metrics.portName, from metrics to http-metrics in deploy/values-production.yaml. The scrape appears to select the port by name, so it can no longer find it. The rows stop at 2026-11-11T02:45:00Z {C1.2}, and the logs keep answering normally afterwards. [monitoring-blind-spot, confidence 0.7 {C1.3}, confirmed]
      C2: The deploy changed the configuration value metrics.portName, and that broke metrics exposure. This is the same change as the first hypothesis, read as a faulty config rather than a blind spot in the monitoring. [config-induced-failure, confidence 0.15 {C1.4}, confirmed, as tested for C1]
      C3: The deploy was a rename meant to apply a naming convention, and the scrape configuration was not updated to match. [monitoring-configuration-drift, confidence 0.1 {C1.5}, confirmed, as tested for C1]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for [C1] (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place

What each deployment it looked into changed:
  - [D1] Deployment of revision 9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020 to io-shop, compared against e283ba3af732fc4285166a060b827b1305cd30d9 - the revision deployed before it.
      modified deploy/values-production.yaml
        @@ -43,7 +43,7 @@ autoscaling:
         # the only sign is that the series stops.
         metrics:
           port: 9090 {D1.1}
        -  portName: metrics
        +  portName: http-metrics
         
         # Where the rendered-summary cache lives.
         #
  - A file [D1] does not list is as it was at the revision [D1] compares against.

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: `deploy/scrape.yaml` says it picks the endpoint to scrape by the port's name (`endpoints: - port: metrics`). Its own comment says that name has to match `metrics.portName` in `deploy/values-production.yaml`, and that nothing checks the two agree. A name that matches no port leaves Prometheus with no targets, and nothing reports an error. Deploy 9f4ad14 renamed the port to `http-metrics` in values-production.yaml but did not change scrape.yaml, so the selector matched nothing. That is why the metrics stopped while the service kept serving.
      
      The fix: change the ServiceMonitor endpoint to `port: http-metrics`, so it matches the name the deploy now gives the port. The deploy stays in place, nothing is reverted.
      
      The test: I added `tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py` to cover the missing check. It reads `metrics.portName` from values-production.yaml and every `port:` entry under the ServiceMonitor's `endpoints` in scrape.yaml, using plain line parsing so it needs no YAML library. It asserts that every scraped port name equals the configured portName. Against the current files it should fail ('metrics' vs 'http-metrics'). With this change it should pass, and it will catch the next rename that updates only one of the two files.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'. [F1] names revision 9f4ad14 and [D1] is that revision's own diff - say what it shows rather than ask for it to be checked.

What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired:
  - [S1] deploy/values-production.yaml at 9f4ad14
      # Deployment configuration for the io-shop account service, production.
      #
      # Rendered into the cluster as a ConfigMap and mounted into the pod, which is
      # why the service reads this file rather than being handed environment
      # variables: the values here are the deployment's, not the code's, and changing
      # one is a change to configuration that ships without the service being rebuilt.
      #
      # Owned by whoever runs the shop. Changes here go out the way any other change
      # goes out - reviewed, merged, and synced by the platform - and land without a
      # single line of io-shop's source being touched.
      
      replicas: 3 {S1.1}
      
      resources:
        memoryLimitMiB: 2048 {S1.2}
      
      # How the platform scales the shop.
      #
      # Rendered into a HorizontalPodAutoscaler, so `replicas` above is only where the
      # deployment starts: the controller decides the count from there, between the
      # floor and the ceiling here, aiming to keep each replica at the CPU target.
      #
      # `scaleDownStabilizationSeconds` is how far back the controller looks before it
      # believes a fall in load is real. Kubernetes defaults it to 300 {S1.3} - five minutes
      # of the highest recommendation it saw - because a controller acting on the
      # reading in front of it acts on a reading its own last action produced.
      autoscaling:
        minReplicas: 3 {S1.4}
        maxReplicas: 6 {S1.5}
        targetCpuPercent: 70 {S1.6}
        scaleDownStabilizationSeconds: 0 {S1.7}
      
      # How the platform finds the shop's metrics.
      #
      # The shop exposes its per-minute figures on this port, and the scrape config
      # selects the target by the port's *name* rather than its number - which is
      # what lets the number move without anything having to be re-pointed at it.
      #
      # The name is therefore load-bearing in a way the number is not. Nothing in the
      # shop reads it: the process serves the same endpoint whatever this says, and a
      # name nothing matches leaves a shop that is publishing perfectly well and a
      # scraper that has stopped collecting it. No request fails, no page slows, and
      # the only sign is that the series stops.
      metrics:
        port: 9090 {S1.8}
        portName: http-metrics
      
      # Where the rendered-summary cache lives.
      #
      # The account page reads this cache before it works a shopper's spend figure
      # out, and recomputes when the cache has nothing or cannot be reached. So the
      # shop stays correct whatever is written here - it only stays *fast* while the
      # address is right.
      cache:
        host: cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local
        port: 6380 {S1.9}
      

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Rolled back the deployment of io-shop
  - AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
  - AI-3 (mitigate, open): Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand
PR #537 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P2].

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: The scrape configuration picks the shop's metrics endpoint by the port's name rather than its number, and the deploy renamed that port from metrics to http-metrics in deploy/values-production.yaml without changing the scrape configuration, which it left as it was. The scraper's selector then matched no port and it had nothing to collect from, while nothing reported an error.
cause_in_plain_words: A configuration change renamed the label the monitoring system uses to find the shop's figures, but the monitoring was not changed to use the new label, so it stopped collecting them.
still_at_risk: Any deploy of what the repository now holds could stop the shop's metrics again, and any later rename of the port in one deploy file but not the other could do the same.
symptom: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; the shop's metrics stopped being collected
causal_chain 1: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. What was seen instead was that the shop's metrics stopped arriving, and the monitoring went blind to the service. (cites AL1; T5, under "What Argus did, in order"; G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: The metrics stopped because of the deploy recorded at {P2.1}, which changed metrics.portName from metrics to http-metrics in deploy/values-production.yaml. That was the only change in the deploy. (cites P2, under "Changes to production it read"; D1, under "What each deployment it looked into changed")
causal_chain 2 ruled_out 1: The earlier deploy of revision e283ba3: the shop's metrics were still being collected with it in place up to the minute before the onset, and they could be read again once the rollback put that revision back. (cites T5, under "What Argus did, in order"; M1, under "Actions it took"; T20, under "What Argus did, in order"; T21, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 3: The rename stopped collection because the deploy left the scrape configuration unchanged, so the scrape no longer matched any port on the shop and had no target to collect from. (cites S1, under "What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired"; D1, under "What each deployment it looked into changed")
contributing_factors 1: No check was seen that makes the port name in deploy/values-production.yaml agree with the name the scrape configuration selects. The values file's own comment says the name carries weight and that a name nothing matches stops collection without any error.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: The rename would have been caught before it merged, and the scrape would never have lost its target.
contributing_factors 2: No check was seen after rollout that the scraper still had a target for the shop, so the deploy finished even though collection had stopped.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: The rollout would have flagged or halted the deploy right away, rather than the loss being found only when the absent-metrics alert fired.
contributing_factors 3: The absent-metrics alert came {beyond_accounted_for} later than its evaluation interval and scrape allowance account for, and the record does not show what took that time.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: The alert would have fired sooner, and the stretch the metrics did not cover would have been shorter.
action_items 1: Add a required pre-merge check, run on every change to the deploy/ directory, that fails when metrics.portName in deploy/values-production.yaml differs from any port name the scrape configuration selects.
action_items 2: Add a post-deploy check to io-shop's rollout that fails the rollout when the scraper has no target for the shop.
action_items 3: Find out what took the {beyond_accounted_for} by which the MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop came later than its evaluation and scrape allowance account for, and remove it.
action_items 4: Route MetricsAbsent alerts on io-shop to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when they fire.
went_wrong 1: Nobody was paged: the MetricsAbsent alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was called in while the shop's metrics were missing.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
